heading: The Okanagan in December, 2026
title: The Okanagan in December 2026 | Okanagan Roam
description: Things to do in the Okanagan in December 2026: holiday theatre, concerts, New Year's Eve, ski hills and outdoor rinks, saunas, and cozy food for cold days.
intro: December is when the Okanagan turns to winter. The ski hills are up and running, outdoor rinks freeze over in town, and the theatres fill with holiday shows. The valley stays quieter than the mountains, so it's an easy month to mix a ski day with a show, a sauna and a long dinner.

This guide picks a handful of December events, then adds the mountains, skating, indoor warm-ups and cozy food. For every holiday market, light-up and Christmas concert, see our {page:/guides/okanagan-holiday-events|holiday events guide}, our {page:/guides/okanagan-christmas-markets|Christmas markets guide} and our {page:/guides/okanagan-winter-events|winter events guide}. Every dated event is also on {page:/whats-on|What's On}.

sections.heading: On the calendar in December
sections.lead: Theatre, dance and music through the month, from a farm-field hockey show to a sing-along Messiah.

items.name: Le Hockey Sweater
items.text: Caravan Farm Theatre's winter show, a joyful, raucous take on Roch Carrier's The Hockey Sweater that brings an outdoor hockey game to the farm's fields and forests. There are several performances a day. Tickets are $57.75 to $73.50.

items.name: Anne of Green Gables
items.text: New Vintage Theatre's annual holiday play at the Rotary Centre for the Arts, with a cast of local talent in an all-ages production.

items.name: Laila Biali: Wintersongs at The Dream
items.text: the Grammy-nominated jazz singer and pianist plays songs from her holiday album Wintersongs, as a duo with bassist Jodi Proznick, at 7 pm.

items.name: Handel's Messiah Live
items.text: the Okanagan Festival Singers close their 40th-anniversary season with a sing-along Messiah at 7 pm, where the audience is invited to join in. Admission is $15.

items.name: The Nutcracker – Canadian School of Ballet
items.text: the holiday classic at Kelowna Community Theatre, with guest dancers from Miami City Ballet. There are matinee and evening shows.

items.name: Little Women: The Broadway Musical
items.text: the musical version of the four March sisters' story at Vernon's historic Powerhouse Theatre. A heartfelt holiday-season show for families and musical fans.

sections.heading: A few lights and markets
sections.lead: Only a small sample here. The full lists are in the {page:/guides/okanagan-holiday-events|holiday events} and {page:/guides/okanagan-christmas-markets|Christmas markets} guides.

items.name: Enderby Christmas Light-Up & Parade
items.text: downtown Enderby lights up with a free Christmas parade and festive evening from 5:30 pm. A cheerful small-town start to the holidays.

items.name: East Kelowna Christmas in the Country Market
items.text: more than 70 local artisans, crafters and bakers inside the historic East Kelowna Hall. Entry is a loonie or toonie, and proceeds support the hall.

items.name: Winter Solstice Light-Up Trail Nights
items.text: Riding 4 Life Ranch lights up its trail course from 5 pm. Ride your own horse through it ($20) or just come for the fire, a warm drink and a treat.

items.name: Valley First New York New Year's 2026
items.text: a free, all-ages party at the Stuart Park rink from 6 pm, with live bands, skating, food trucks and an early fireworks countdown at 9 pm. Made for families who want to ring in the year before bedtime.

items.name: Next Stop Comedy at Unleashed Brewing
items.text: stand-up comedy in the North End at 8 pm, with a New Year's Eve show.

sections.heading: First turns on the mountain
sections.lead: Big White and SilverStar list their 2026/27 seasons as starting in late November, so both should be running through December, snow permitting. Apex and Baldy run in winter only; check their listings for opening dates. Our {page:/guides/ski-season-big-white-silverstar|Big White and SilverStar guide} and {page:/guides/apex-baldy-ski-guide|Apex and Baldy guide} cover lifts, lessons and where to eat.

items.name: Big White Ski Resort
items.text: the Okanagan's big mountain resort, with 2,834 acres of patrolled terrain. The season runs November 26, 2026 to April 4, 2027, and from December 18 the resort runs the largest night-skiing operation in Western Canada. Free Snow Host tours leave the Village Centre at 10:15 each morning.

items.name: SilverStar Mountain Resort
items.text: 133 runs on 3,304 acres, with night skiing on Friday and Saturday nights. The My1Pass day ticket also covers cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, fat biking, skating and tubing. The alpine season runs November 27, 2026 to April 4, 2027.

items.name: Apex Mountain Resort
items.text: Penticton's home mountain, a 30-minute drive from town, with 85 runs. Friday and Saturday nights bring night skiing, night tubing and the skating loop under lights from 4 to 9 pm. It runs in winter only.

items.name: Baldy Mountain Resort
items.text: a small, friendly family hill known for its tree runs and short lift lines. New this winter is cat skiing to Baldy's upper terrain, Friday to Sunday. The access road turns to gravel near the top, and winter tires are strongly recommended.

items.name: Big White Winter Rally
items.text: rally cars compete on winter roads in the Big White area. Check the official spectator guide for viewing spots and road closures.

items.name: The Loose Moose Challenge – December
items.text: a family scavenger hunt across Big White's blue runs. Pick up an adventure card at the Events Tent in the Village Centre from 10 am.

items.name: Salomon Holiday Rail Jam at SilverStar
items.text: skiers and snowboarders show off on a custom rail setup while a DJ plays, from 2:30 pm. Free to watch.

sections.heading: Skating and snow days
sections.lead: Outdoor ice depends on the weather, so check each listing before you go. Our {page:/guides/okanagan-skating|skating guide} lists every rink and arena.

items.name: Stuart Park Outdoor Rink
items.text: a free outdoor rink on the downtown waterfront, with Okanagan Lake and the Bennett Bridge behind it. It opens in early December, weather permitting, and a rental hut has skates and helmets.

items.name: Penticton Outdoor Skating Rink (Gyro Park)
items.text: a free family rink at the foot of Martin Street, near the beach and downtown cafés. The park's holiday lights are up from early December. There are no rentals, so bring skates and a helmet.

items.name: Vernon Recreation Complex – Priest Valley Arena & Centennial Outdoor Rink
items.text: the Centennial Outdoor Rink is free from December through February, weather permitting, and the indoor arena next door has public skating. Bring skates: there are no rentals.

items.name: Happy Valley Ice Skating Rink – Big White
items.text: what the resort calls Canada's highest outdoor skating rink, lit for night skating, with a bonfire beside it every afternoon after 3 pm. The Tube Park and Twinkling Trail are next door.

sections.heading: Warm up indoors
sections.lead: After a cold day outside, head in for heat, water and a museum or two. Our {page:/guides/okanagan-saunas-spas|saunas & spas guide} and {page:/guides/rainy-day-okanagan|rainy-day guide} have more.

items.name: Löyly Floating Sauna
items.text: a Finnish-style cedar sauna floating at the Downtown Marina, with a lake cold plunge and a warm solarium lounge over Okanagan Lake. Book an 80-minute community session online, since walk-ins aren't guaranteed space.

items.name: Penticton Community Centre (Pool & Lazy River)
items.text: a leisure pool with a lazy river and waterslide during Public Swim, plus a big whirlpool, sauna and steam room for warming up on a cold day.

items.name: Kelowna Curling Club
items.text: one-hour Try Curling sessions with an instructor and all equipment supplied, about $25 a person, booked online.

items.name: Okanagan Heritage Museum
items.text: the natural and human history of the Okanagan, from syilx culture to settler life, with exhibits such as Dinosaurs of BC. The second Sunday of each month is pay-what-you-wish.

items.name: Okanagan Science Centre
items.text: hands-on exhibits, planetarium shows and live animals in Polson Park. Just drop in and pay at the front desk; planetarium shows need pre-registration.

sections.heading: Cozy food and drink
sections.lead: Fireplaces, fondue, books and board games for short, cold days. Our {page:/guides/cozy-spots-okanagan|cozy spots guide} and {page:/guides/soup-ramen-pho-okanagan|soup, ramen and pho guide} have more.

items.name: Grate Cheesery
items.text: a wine-and-cheese bar run by a passionate cheesemonger. Book one of the fondue nights, or trust the curated pairings.

items.name: Pulp Fiction – Pandosy
items.text: a coffee house that doubles as a rare and used bookstore, with a cozy, vintage feel. Order the coffee milkshake and browse the shelves.

items.name: The Boarding House Cafe
items.text: a family-friendly board game café with more than 300 games. Order a hot chocolate, pick a game and settle in for a proper game night.

items.name: Kaze Japanese Restaurant
items.text: a family-run spot in a converted old home, with a fireplace in the dining room. Reviewers call the miso ramen spectacular.

items.name: Gusto Ferrari
items.text: a small Italian deli and restaurant that makes everything from scratch. Order the homemade pasta or the wood-fired margherita pizza.

items.name: Campo Marina
items.text: a cozy downtown Italian spot that stays busy. The house focaccia alone is worth the visit, and portions are generous.

items.lead: Valley and mountain are two different winters:
items.tip: the valley towns are often grey and cool in December, while the ski hills are much colder and snowier. Pack for both if you plan to do both.
roads up to the ski hills can be snowy and icy. Drive with winter-ready tires, leave extra time and check road conditions before you go.
many wineries, patios and seasonal attractions cut back from November to April, and some places close over the holidays. Check each listing's hours, and call ahead if a stop matters.

items.lead: Outdoor ice and snow are weather-dependent:
items.tip: rinks, tube parks and ski runs can close in a warm spell or a storm. Have an indoor backup.
popular shows, saunas and holiday-week dinners fill up. Book ahead where a listing says to.
December days are the shortest of the year, so put drives and outdoor stops early in the day.
